prompts.A:
Create ONE polished full-screen mobile app design proposal for Hangul Sori, German UI, Korean-learning game “Wortkette” (끝말잇기). Portrait aspect ratio exactly 402:874, edge-to-edge flat screenshot, no phone bezel, no perspective camera, no multiple screens, no labels outside the UI. Use the attached approved Wörter-Quiz only as the source of material identity: rich deep emerald/jade textured header, warm ivory hanji, natural dark walnut, thin restrained warm gold edges, physically grounded raised faces and contact shadows, cream serif display typography. This is a DIFFERENT game mechanic and a DIFFERENT body design: a word-chain workbench, never a quiz answer stack, matching grid, flip card, book, scroll or card holder.

COMPOSITION: Keep the top header compact, height about 112 of the 874 logical units. Left cream back chevron with a generous touch area; small centered HANGUL SORI brand; large centered “Wortkette” beneath it. NO cloud artwork, NO gear icon, NO coins, NO mascot, NO decorative logo glyph. Below header, the warm hanji game surface has a readable subtitle “Letzte Silbe → nächstes Wort”. A compact status row reads “Du bist dran” at left and a modest outlined timer at right. Then a quiet horizontal history rail: small prior-word blocks connected in reading order by short thin connectors, and small exact chain count. The current word is the primary visual hero: individual large fixed Korean syllable blocks seated side by side in a shallow walnut writing rail. Light ivory/wood faces for all earlier syllables; deep emerald face and cream glyph ONLY for the last syllable. These are read-only syllable markers, not draggable or selectable answer buttons. The current word's exact German meaning is clearly readable beneath the rail, followed by a real audio control labeled “Anhören” with speaker icon and a separate compact “1×” TTS speed control; both have an apparent 48dp or larger face.

Below, show the exact instruction “Beginne mit »SYLLABLE«”, making the required Korean syllable easy to find without decorative arrows crossing text. Then one wide recessed ivory typing field, warm wooden edge, width roughly 338 logical units, height at least 64, showing the specified placeholder or draft. Under it, one wide raised emerald “Senden” button with a small send arrow. The input and submit feel like one working area. Korean text is correctly formed, large and crisp; German labels retain umlauts, punctuation and exact spelling. No second CTA, no alternative answer cards, no correctness judgments, no streak, no score, no XP or invented learner progress.

SHARED SHELL CONSTRAINT: Reserve the bottom exactly 82 of 874 logical units as a plain deep emerald navigation shelf with a very fine warm gold top rule. Keep it COMPLETELY EMPTY: no icons, no icon placeholders, no circles, no text, no home glyph, no five invented drawings. The approved five image icons will be placed later in Figma from exact original files. This intentional empty dock must appear in the output. Also leave at least 16 logical units clear between the last interactive button/shadow and the top of the dock. Do not reproduce the reference image's cloud, gear, coins or navigation icons. No new character. No tutorial arrows. Keyboard is dismissed in this composition; do not draw a keyboard. Do not add title A/B/C, CEFR badges, developer notes or “placeholder” text anywhere. Maintain useful spacing of 8–16 logical units, high contrast, readable hierarchy and realistic layered materials; avoid excessive blank paper or giant ornament.
EXACT CONTENT FOR THIS SINGLE SCREEN: history in left-to-right chronological order “가방”; count “Kette: 1”; timer “30s”; current word “가방” divided into 2 fixed syllable blocks exactly “가 | 방”, with ONLY “방” as the final emerald block. Meaning “Tasche”. Instruction “Beginne mit »방«”. Input is empty and displays the subdued placeholder “Wort auf Koreanisch …”. Keep all text exactly. Every syllable must appear once in the current-word rail and in correct order.
